segments.text: For most of my career, I never questioned vaccine safety.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03

segments.text: Like many doctors, I assumed FDA approval and public recommendations meant that vaccines were evaluated and regulated essentially the same way as any other medication.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03

segments.text: But over time, I learned that this is not entirely the case.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03

segments.text: During COVID, I watched legitimate scientific debate
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03

segments.text: around treatment narrow dramatically and questions that would normally be discussed openly in medicine were discouraged.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03

segments.text: And it prompted me to look more closely at how policy and regulation and liability intersect in public health.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03

segments.text: That's when I learned about a law that Congress passed called the National Childhood Vaccine Injury Act of 1986.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03

segments.text: This law grants vaccine manufacturers broad protection from traditional lawsuits.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03

segments.text: As a result, when someone is seriously injured following a vaccination, they generally cannot bring a case before a jury or go after the manufacturer through the normal justice system.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03

segments.text: Instead, injured patients are directed to a separate process.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03

segments.text: It's called the Vaccine Injury Compensation Program, BICP.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03

segments.text: And this program was created to provide compensation without requiring proof of fault.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03

segments.text: but it also operates differently from the civil courts.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03

segments.text: Claimants have limited access to discovery and compensation is paid from a trust fund rather than the manufacturer itself.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03

segments.text: Since the VIC program began, it has paid more than $5 billion to almost 10,000 individuals.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03

segments.text: Manufacturers argued for this protection by pointing out that vaccines, like many medical products, can carry unavoidable risks for some people
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03

segments.text: even when they're properly manufactured and administered.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03

segments.text: And manufacturers maintained that this legal structure was necessary to ensure a stable vaccine supply.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03

segments.text: That history matters because no other category of pharmaceutical products is treated this way under the law.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03

segments.text: Civil liability is not about assigning blame.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03

segments.text: It's one of the key mechanisms our system has to encourage rigorous testing and transparency and continuous safety improvement.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03

segments.text: But when that mechanism is limited, the incentives change and product quality and public confidence can suffer.

segments.text: If a medical product is truly safe and truly effective, it should be able to withstand scrutiny under the same legal standards that apply to other medications.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
